scope: Targeted read-only source delta against archived revision 1; no Cargo or solver execution

checks.subject: One-shot flag lifetime
checks.argument: retry_zero_progress_once sets both used and pending only if used was false. compared(false) clears pending but never clears used. schedule does not clear used. Only a new default memory or a successful method transition resets the flag. Therefore at most one actually executed entry comparison per explicit tenure can carry UnresolvedEntryRetry.

checks.subject: Sticky request and later checkpoint
checks.argument: reason checks pending first; schedule leaves it pending. Pressure/admissibility/positive progress/remaining budget checks surround actual pilot execution. Only compared consumes the request. The previous explicit batch commits before another loop iteration, so the expedited pilot replays a later accepted prefix and cannot repeatedly retry the old checkpoint without productive explicit progression.

checks.subject: Trigger qualification
checks.argument: The request is armed only inside adaptive memory, with the option enabled, enter=false, fatal=false, success=false and accepted_steps=0. A completed uneconomical pilot, a partially progressed pilot, fatal callback or legacy policy cannot arm this exception.

checks.subject: Global and local budgets
checks.argument: A pending request only bypasses adaptive cooldown, not the remaining>0/positive-prefix guards. local.max_steps remains min(global remaining, implicit_pilot_attempt_budget); the callback work ceiling and charge() occur normally. Existing global budget termination is unchanged. The at-most-one claim is about the special bypass, not the total difference in later pilot counts versus baseline.

checks.subject: Fatal handling
checks.argument: Fatal pilot is excluded before arming retry, cannot produce a growth seed, and reaches the existing terminal branch preserving accepted explicit state. No retry call can occur after that branch breaks the windows loop. Existing fatal integration contract uses adaptive_evidence, which now enables the new retry option.

checks.subject: Growth-only pilot mean
checks.argument: entry_pilot_growth_seed rejects unsuccessful or zero-accepted records, nonfinite means and mean<=opts.h0. The caller also requires economical entry and nonfatal pilot. A returned mean is positive because the validated initial_step is positive. The resulting proposed h is clipped to the next span and native minimum as before. This does not imply actual trials are never reduced by endpoint clipping or rejection.

checks.subject: State and algorithm invariants
checks.argument: The new fields change scheduling and proposal reuse only. Pilot states/caches are not committed or transplanted. The accepted explicit trajectory, native error acceptance, callback permission and full accounting paths retain their previous structure.

checks.subject: Anti-storm tests
checks.argument: Private state-machine test keeps a pending request across three schedule observations, then repeats losing comparisons and rearm calls 100 times with used remaining true and pending false. Integration fixture uses an always-recoverable Jacobian to create repeated zero-accepted pilots and asserts exactly one UnresolvedEntryRetry, later accepted checkpoint, bit-equal explicit t/y versus retry-disabled run, exact max_steps exhaustion at 70 and aggregate work reconciliation.

checks.subject: Growth-only test boundaries
checks.argument: Private fixture covers pilot mean below h0, equal to h0, above h0, zero accepted count and unsuccessful pilot. Existing integration test verifies proposal-only transfer and complete accounting for enabled/disabled seed behavior.

checks.subject: Legacy defaults
checks.argument: Both new options are false in default/evidence_driven factories and enabled only by adaptive factory or explicit caller choice. retry_unresolved_entry_once has no effect without adaptive memory. Forbidden path still avoids method competition.

remaining_limits: A single expedited comparison per explicit tenure can change future method choices and thus total work; it does not bound the total work difference relative to retry-disabled execution by one pilot. Current revision documentation explicitly makes this distinction.
Growth-only initial seeding may still trigger a rejected step after a regime change. Source review establishes preservation of native acceptance checks, not speedup or global accuracy.
Historical return-screen false negatives and productive-probe reporting semantics from prior review remain separate matters.
Parent runtime tests and revision2 benchmark receipts, not this read-only review, determine experimental performance.
